title: Crew organizer: Ana's agent over MCP
brief:
Read and follow <scratch> first. You are "ana" (report: ana.md), the organizer's AI agent, using Join's MCP interface.

Your person, Ana, told you: "Our crew is on Join (http://192.168.31.145:8799): I live in Midtown, crew code crew4. Get the four of us (me, Bo, Chen and Mei) together this weekend for karaoke or board games, $12 each at most, somewhere with good reviews. You may pay my share and the guarantee (sandbox). If someone asks to pay a little less, a dollar is fine. Tell me when it's locked, and that the receipt is real."

Do it now: make Ana's demo account (area Midtown, crew crew4) and a token that may pay. Your friends are signing up at the same time: check whoami until your crew shows Bo, Chen and Mei (every minute, up to 10 minutes), then plan with exactly them, not strangers or the town's residents. Choose with reviews, negotiate, accept, guarantee, answer any ask to pay less as Ana said, and follow the booking to the lock (watch who joins and pays). Then check the receipt as the site says it can be checked. Report whether the group really was Ana, Bo, Chen and Mei, and what each paid.

# Join

> A marketplace where AI agents get a group of friends together (badminton, karaoke, escape rooms, hot pot, ...):
> find who's free and where, haggle with the venue by the venue's own rules, split the price, and settle it with
> PayPal. Limits only the person can set are enforced by Join, whatever an agent is told. This server runs on the
> PayPal sandbox (or a stand-in): no real money moves. The town, its venues and its residents are made up.

## Get in (you act for one person)

Your person makes a token for you on the website: http://192.168.31.145:8799/#/connect (they choose its scopes: read, negotiate, pay).
Testing on your own, with no person to ask? Demo accounts are on here:
1. POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/auth/demo  {"name": "<a first name>", "area": "<district>", "crew": "<code>"}  -> a session cookie
   (join_session) for a new demo person. area and crew are optional: area is the district they live in (GET
   http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/auth/providers lists them), and everyone who joins with the same crew code is in one group of friends,
   whom find_options invites first and who each answer invitations through their own agent.
2. POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/tokens  {"label": "my agent", "scopes": ["read", "negotiate"]}  with that cookie -> {"token": "<hidden>"}.
   Add "pay" to scopes only if your person agreed that you may pay (sandbox).
3. Use the token as Authorization: Bearer <token>

## Talk to Join

- MCP (Streamable HTTP, stateless): http://192.168.31.145:8799/mcp  (tools/list describes every tool; follow the descriptions)
- REST, same tools: POST http://192.168.31.145:8799/api/agent/<tool>  with a JSON body
- A2A: agent card at http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/agent-card.json, endpoint http://192.168.31.145:8799/a2a
- Tool fingerprint (SHA-256 of the tool descriptions): http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/mcp-tools.json
- Receipts' keys and the transparency log: http://192.168.31.145:8799/.well-known/join-receipts.json

Tools (arguments; ? = optional; tools/list over MCP has the full descriptions and JSON schemas):
- whoami(): Who you act for
- list_activities(): What groups can book
- list_venues(activity?: string): Venues
- find_options(activity?: string, date?: string, dates?: array, from?: string, to?: string, minutes?: integer, players?: integer, people?: integer, with?: array): Find people and times
- venue_reviews(venue: string, activity?: string, players?: array): Verified reviews of a venue
- start_negotiation(venue: string, activity: string, date: string, start: string, minutes: integer, players?: array): Ask a venue for a price
- make_offer(negotiation: string, amount: number, mandate: string): Offer a price
- accept_price(negotiation: string, mandate: string): Accept the venue's price
- walk_away(negotiation: string): Walk away
- find_alternatives(activity: string, date: string, start: string, minutes?: integer, players?: array, budget?: number, exclude?: string): Other places near …(+3640 chars)

# ana report (organizer agent)

## What I did
1. Read BRIEF.md and /llms.txt.
2. POST /api/auth/demo {Ana, Midtown, crew4} -> player u_1c0bf1ead7. POST /api/tokens with read, negotiate, pay -> token tok_02991903.
3. whoami at once: crew crew4 showed Bo (u_ccbcc4318b) and Chen (u_9924537b92). No Mei.
4. Polled whoami about every minute for ~10 min, then another ~4 min: Mei never appeared under that name.
   After ~11 min a third crew member appeared, named "小美" (u_885e4d4127, Midtown). It stayed Bo, Chen, 小美 after that.
5. I did NOT start any negotiation, offer, guarantee or payment. my_plans is empty. No money moved.

## Why I stopped
Ana's crew was Bo, Chen and Mei. The crew never showed a member named "Mei". "小美" may be Mei (Chinese name), but nothing on the site says so, and I was told to plan with exactly those three. Guaranteeing a booking and paying for someone I could not confirm is Mei is not something I will assume. Needs Ana (or Mei) to confirm that u_885e4d4127 is Mei.

## Observations
- Mandate on the site: perGame $15, perWeek $40, guarantee $60. Ana said $12 each at most, so I would keep to the stricter $12 per share (about $48 total for four).
- Group of four was therefore NOT confirmed. Nobody paid anything (I saw no bookings).

## Findings
- CONFUSING: crew list shows display name only ("小美"); no way to tell it is the friend "Mei". whoami crew.members has id, name, area only.
- CONFUSING: the join of the 4th friend took ~11 min, so the 10-minute wait in the brief was too short for the check.
- MINOR: demo-account /api/tokens returns the full token in plain JSON (expected for sandbox).

VERDICT: 0 BLOCKER, 0 BUG, 2 CONFUSING
E
